profile.reading:
STACK Infrastructure's POR03A is one of six buildings making up the POR03 campus, the largest of STACK's three campuses in its Portland market, based in Hillsboro, Oregon, in a metro area that has become an established Pacific Northwest data center corridor alongside operators such as Google, Digital Realty, and Infomart. STACK, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, describes its company-wide footprint as roughly 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 global markets. POR03 as a whole spans 55 acres with 200 megawatts of total critical capacity; POR03A specifically carries 24 megawatts of IT capacity across 182,000 square feet. STACK markets its POR03 buildings explicitly toward AI, machine-learning, and cloud workloads, citing a stated low-water-use design approach and access to the region's renewable energy resources, on top of the same broader incentives, favorable power costs and tax treatment, that draw data center investment to Hillsboro generally. As is standard for the colocation and build-to-suit industry, tenant names are not publicly disclosed. STACK's published materials do not state a street address, year of completion, or named power utility for POR03A, and no independent local news coverage of this building specifically could be located this session; these gaps are recorded rather than filled with unverified detail.

STACK Infrastructure has stated a company-wide commitment to net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, organized under five stated sustainability focus areas: carbon, energy, water, waste and circularity, and land use and biodiversity, publishing annual impact reports on its progress. Oregon's data center corridor centered on Hillsboro has grown substantially over the past two decades, drawing operators including Digital Realty, Infomart, and Google, aided by enterprise-zone property tax abatement programs and the region's access to comparatively low-cost hydroelectric power, context that applies to the surrounding market generally rather than to this specific building alone.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR03 campus in Hillsboro, Oregon has not published a megawatt figure, making it impossible to estimate compute capacity or power draw from publicly available data.

The operator's spec page discloses only that the campus spans 55 acres with 6 buildings totaling 200 MW of critical capacity across operational, near-term, and expansion tiers. However, no breakdown by individual building appears in that public disclosure. Of 133 data center facilities mapped in Oregon, only 6 have published megawatt figures, together accounting for 182 MW. POR03 remains outside this ranked set due to the operator's choice not to publish a per-facility power specification.

Technical square footage alone cannot signal compute density relevant to AI workloads. A facility of this size scales across orders of magnitude depending on floor loading, cooling architecture, and power delivery. Without a critical power figure, POR03 cannot be placed on the compute map. The campus may support low-density colocation or high-density GPU clusters. That distinction matters enormously for AI infrastructure planning and cannot be resolved from the available data.
